lesson_intro: Welcome to the Speed & Accuracy engine of SSC. The Number System is the foundation of everything in Quantitative Aptitude. In SSC, you don't just solve the problem; you solve it in 20 seconds. Today we focus on 'Divisibility Rules' and 'Unit Digit' calculations. These are not just topics; they are 'Elimination Tools'. If you know a number must be divisible by 11, you can often find the answer among options without solving the whole equation. Let's master the patterns that toppers use to sprint through the paper.

lesson_pages.intro: Today you will study SSC QA: Number System — Divisibility & Unit Digit. By the end, you should clearly understand the main subtopics below and be ready for recall cards and exam practice.

lesson_pages.intro: In aptitude questions, the formula is only the first step. The exam checks whether you can identify the data type and apply the rule quickly.
lesson_pages.title: Divisibility Rules: The Speed Tools

blocks.text: 2: Last digit even. 3: Sum of digits div by 3. 4: Last 2 digits div by 4. 5: Last digit 0 or 5. 8: Last 3 digits div by 8. 9: Sum of digits div by 9. 11: (Sum of digits at odd places) - (Sum of digits at even places): 0...
blocks.title: Divisibility Rules: The Speed Tools

items.label: Cycle of 4
items.value: The unit digit of a number raised to a power repeats every 4 powers

items.label: Note
items.value: 0, 1, 5, 6 always remain same regardless of power

blocks.text: Natural(1, 2..), Whole(0, 1..), Integers(..-1, 0, 1..), Rational(p/q), Irrational(√2, π). Prime numbers: 1 to 100 has 25 prime numbers. 1 is neither prime nor composite. 2 is the only even prime.

quick_note_cards.back: (Sum of digits at odd places) - (Sum of digits at even places) must be 0 or a multiple of 11. (e.g., 1331: (1+3)-(3+1): 0. Divisible!).
